newsitem.title: USA: Dayton Hudson sees 'successful' end to 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dayton Hudson sees 'successful' end to 1996.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Tuesday it expects a successful finish to the year, despite a shorter than usual holiday shopping season between Thanksgiving and Christmas.
"While the holiday calendar is challenging, we believe we are well positioned for a successful finish to 1996," Bob Ulrich, chairman, said in a statement.

Earlier, Dayton Hudson reported operating earnings for the third quarter ended November 2 of $0.51 a primary share and $0.49 fully diluted, before a $9.0 million debt redemption charge. A year ago, it earned $0.18 a share.
"Our third quarter results reflect continued strong profit performance at Target and Mervyn's," Ulrich said.

Dayton said Target's operating profit in the third quarter rose 82 percent to $213 million, compared with $117 million in the same period in 1995. Target's total revenues increased 14 percent and comparable-store revenues were up five percent.
Dayton said Target's gross margin rate improved due to higher merchandise price markups and promotional markdowns.

Dayton said Mervyn's operating profit increased 98 percent in third quarter 1996 to $64 million, compared with $33 million in third quarter 1995. Revenues, however, decreased three percent and comparable-store revenues were down four percent.
Mervyn's operating expenses improved significantly due to reductions in marketing costs, store expense and headquarters costs.

Third quarter operating profit at the Department Store Division declined to $45 million, compared with $50 million in 1995. Total revenues increased one percent compared with last year and comparable-store revenues were down five percent.

The Department Stores' gross margin rate decreased due to the exit of the electronics business and other factors. The operating expenses were reduced due to ongoing initiatives, including lower marketing costs.

Dayton said it took a LIFO inventory charge of $5.0 million in the third quarter, compared with no charge a year ago. Net interest expense for the quarter rose $3.0 million compared with the 1995 period.
